stem: A technician is highly confident about the pest identity. Does that confidence authorize pesticide selection or application?
choices: High confidence can justify treatment selection when the technician has prior experience with the same pest and the product is labeled for it.
Diagnostic confidence does not create treatment-selection or pesticide-application authority; those remain governed by separate authorization, label, facility, and jurisdictional controls.
High crop-loss risk permits the technician to choose an interim treatment while formal approval is pending.
A product label naming the pest is enough to authorize use if the technician follows the listed rate and PPE.
rationale: Correct identification and confidence in the diagnosis are separate from legal and organizational authority to select or apply a pesticide. Product labeling, licensing, facility authorization, jurisdictional requirements, and assigned role all still govern treatment decisions. A technician may provide evidence and escalate the diagnosis without independently converting that diagnosis into application authority.
